subsystems.name: Substrate
subsystems.role: the hardware that runs the system — currently large accelerator clusters, in principle any physical system with the right causal structure.

subsystems.name: Cognitive architecture
subsystems.role: the overall wiring: which modules process what, and how information flows between them.

subsystems.name: World model
subsystems.role: an internal predictive model of the environment that the system updates as it acts.

subsystems.name: Self-model
subsystems.role: a representation of the system's own state, history and attention — the part most theories treat as central.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and interface
subsystems.role: sensors and actuators that tie the system to a world, whether a robot body or a simulated one.

subsystems.name: Evaluation and probing suite
subsystems.role: tests that try to distinguish genuine internal states from plausible-sounding output.

buildSteps.title: Pick a theory and derive predictions
buildSteps.detail: Theories such as global workspace, integrated information, higher-order and attention-schema accounts disagree sharply, so any attempt starts by committing to one and listing the measurable properties it implies.

buildSteps.title: Build the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Assemble enough recurrent compute and memory bandwidth to hold and update a large, continuously changing internal state.

buildSteps.title: Implement a global broadcast
buildSteps.detail: Many specialised modules compete for access to a limited shared workspace; the winners broadcast their content back to the rest of the system, which is the mechanism global workspace theory says makes information conscious.

buildSteps.title: Train a predictive world model
buildSteps.detail: The system learns by predicting what happens next in video, audio and its own motor commands, building a latent model of the world rather than a lookup table.

buildSteps.title: Add a self-model
buildSteps.detail: A second network tracks the system's own internal states and attention, so the system carries a simplified model of itself alongside its model of the world.

buildSteps.title: Close the sensorimotor loop
buildSteps.detail: Give the system a body or simulated body and let it act continuously, because most candidate theories tie consciousness to ongoing interaction rather than passive processing.

buildSteps.title: Probe for indicator properties
buildSteps.detail: Run tests derived from human and animal neuroscience — recurrent processing, attentional modulation, unified report, integration across modules — and record which pass.

buildSteps.title: Test adversarially
buildSteps.detail: Check whether the system's self-reports actually track its internal states, or are confabulated. Language models describe experience fluently without any verified inner state, so this step is where most claims fail.

buildSteps.title: Attempt the brain-emulation route
buildSteps.detail: A separate path is to map a real brain's wiring and simulate it directly. That avoids needing a theory of consciousness but needs imaging and computing power far beyond today's.

prerequisites.why: global workspace, integrated information and higher-order theories all make some predictions, but a large adversarial test found evidence partly supporting and partly challenging each.
training and running very large recurrent networks is routine, even if it says nothing about whether they are conscious.
the full wiring of a small worm has been mapped; a whole mammalian brain is far out of reach.
there is no agreed measurement that can confirm consciousness in another entity, human or machine.
researchers still disagree on what would count as success, which makes engineering targets hard to set.

pathway.milestone: theories of consciousness translated into indicator checklists applied to existing AI systems
pathway.unlocks: a disciplined way to compare claims instead of judging by how human-like the output sounds.

pathway.milestone: architectures deliberately built around one theory and tested against it
pathway.unlocks: evidence for or against that theory, and clearer ideas about which mechanisms matter.

pathway.milestone: systems whose internal states can be read out and manipulated reliably
pathway.unlocks: experiments that link internal structure to behaviour rather than to words.

pathway.milestone: whole-brain emulation of a small mammal
pathway.unlocks: a system whose consciousness could be argued by analogy, though even then it could not be proven.

pathway.milestone: an artificial system meeting every agreed indicator
pathway.unlocks: no certainty — the problem of knowing another mind may simply persist.
